target: leaf lamina PO_0020039 is not punctate: no dots on the lower surface (negation of PATO_0001512 punctate). PO has no class for the dots themselves. The lamina is present.
fix: 'dots absent', 'without dots', 'not dotted' and 'epunctate' mean a surface has no dots or dashes. Annotate the surface as not punctate (PATO_0001512) or make no annotation. Never record the organ whose description holds the phrase as absent.
reason: Myristicaceae descriptions say whether there are dark dots or dashes on the lower leaf surface. The same lamina is described as greyish or reddish brown below.

target: palea PO_0009038 absent (PATO_0000462) in the sterile basal florets only. The palea of the fertile floret is present and elliptic.
fix: In GrassBase/POWO grass descriptions, 'Basal sterile florets ... without significant palea' puts the absence on the sterile florets. Keep 'sterile floret' as context, and never record 'palea absent' for the taxon when a fertile palea is described.
reason: In Oryza the two reduced sterile lemmas below the fertile floret have no palea. The fertile floret has a well-developed palea.

target: trichome PO_0000282 absent on the leaf, i.e. leaf PO_0025034 glabrous (PATO_0000453). The leaf is present.
fix: In structured 'Character: value' text, 'Hairs: absent' or 'Indumentum: absent' means the hairs (trichome PO_0000282) are absent, i.e. the part is glabrous. Never put the absence on the organ of the enclosing section.
reason: The character name 'Hairs' was dropped, so the absence went to the leaf, which is described as ridged.

target: no annotation. PO has no caudex class, and 'caudex' is only a lexicon synonym of stem PO_0009047. The stem is present and glandular.
fix: Never turn the absence of a narrow synonym (caudex, scape, culm, trunk, cane, primocane) into the absence of the general PO class it is listed under. Give the absence of a proper subclass if one exists, otherwise no annotation.
reason: Eriogonum descriptions say whether there is a woody caudex. The flowering stems are described.

target: cauline leaf PO_0000013 absent. The basal (rosette) leaves PO_0000014 are present and persistent.
fix: 'cauline leaves absent' maps to cauline leaf PO_0000013 absent, and 'basal leaves absent' maps to rosette leaf PO_0000014 absent. Neither ever maps to leaf PO_0025034 absent.
reason: Scapose Draba species have only basal rosette leaves, which are often persistent.

target: leaf sheath auricle PO_0020106 absent, and oral setae (trichome PO_0000282 at the sheath summit) absent. The present record is also wrong: 'longitudinal ribs conspicuous' describes the culm sheath, so it is leaf sheath PO_0020104 ribbed, not stipule.
fix: In bamboo descriptions, 'auricles' means leaf sheath auricle PO_0020106, 'oral setae' means trichome PO_0000282, and 'culm sheath' means leaf sheath PO_0020104. None of them maps to stipule PO_0020041. 'A and B absent' gives one absence for each of A and B.
reason: Fargesia culm sheaths are ribbed and lack auricles and oral setae. Bamboos have no stipules, so both records were wrongly mapped to stipule.

target: leaf lamina PO_0020039 absent from the lower (basal) sheaths only. The foliage leaves have pubescent blades. No taxon-level lamina absence.
fix: In Cyperaceae and Poaceae, 'bladeless' ('lower sheaths bladeless', 'basal sheaths bladeless') limits the absence to the sheaths it names. Apply it only to those bearers, never to the whole taxon when the same description gives blade characters.
reason: Fuirena ciliaris has well-developed hairy blades. Only the lowest sheaths lack blades.

target: no annotation. 'Flowers not known' is a gap in the material, not a phenotype. The axillary (fruiting) inflorescence stays.
fix: '<part> not known / not seen / unknown / not described / not observed / not collected' is a statement about the specimens. It never gives absent (PATO_0000462); drop it.
reason: The species is described from fruiting material only. The inflorescence position comes from the infructescence.

target: 'leafless' describes an axis (the scape or stolons), so make no taxon-level leaf PO_0025034 absence. The leaves are present at anthesis.
fix: When 'leafless' modifies an axis ('scapes leafless', 'stolons leafless', 'stems leafless above'), it describes that axis. Make it a taxon-level leaf absence only when the whole plant is called leafless and no leaves are described anywhere.
reason: The same description says outright that leaves are present at anthesis. Ixeris stolonifera has rosette leaves on leafless flowering stems or stolons.

target: no annotation. 'Flowers not seen' is a gap in the material. The villosulous inflorescence axes stay.

target: leaf lamina PO_0020039 absent from the basal sheaths only (bladeless basal leaf sheaths PO_0020104). The foliage blades are linear.

reason: This is the Carex case cited in docs/km-classification.md: the basal sheaths have no blades and the culm leaves do.

target: no outer bracts at the ostiole (syconium ostiole FLOPO_0986063). There is no general bract absence: the basal bracts PO_0009055 are present and connate into a disc.
fix: In Ficus, 'sans bractées externes' and 'without external (lateral) bracts' refer to the ostiole or the side of the fig. They never mean that every bract is absent; the basal bracts are a separate set.
reason: The description itself has connate basal bracts forming a persistent split, lobed disc.

reason: The puberulous bracts are the basal or ostiolar bracts, a different set from the lateral bracts.

target: no annotation for 'caudex absent'. The present record is also wrong: 'not fistulose' was annotated as hollow. It should be stem PO_0009047 solid, or the negation of hollow.

target: cauline leaf PO_0000013 absent. The rosette leaves PO_0000014 are present; 'sessile' belongs to them (or to the flowers).
